palisade_fileid::hash

Module cache 

Source
Expand description

The hash cache (#46): digests reused while a file is unchanged.

An agent must not rehash a file at every launch. HashCache keeps the digests of each file under its FileKey, and gives them back only while the file’s current key is the same. Any change to a key component is a miss, and the stale entry is dropped.

§What is cached

A CacheValue holds the results by computation tier, each with its own version: the flat hashes (FlatTier) and the Authenticode image digests (ImageTier). When this library changes how a tier is computed, its version constant (FLAT_TIER_VERSION, IMAGE_TIER_VERSION) goes up, and cached tiers of an older version are ignored: only the affected tier is recomputed. The value also records the library version that computed it, the file-type classifier version (#44) and when it was computed.

§Memory bounds

The cache is an LRU bounded by entries and by bytes (CacheConfig; defaults 1,000,000 entries and 256 MiB). Inserting past either bound evicts the least recently used entries first.

§Persisted records and tampering

The agent persists the cache in its local store (#61, ADR 0007). Records leave memory only through HashCache::export and come back only through HashCache::import, as CacheRecords encoded with CacheRecord::encode. Each carries an HMAC-SHA-256 tag (ADR 0008) over every byte, keyed with an agent-held MacKey (#18). A record whose tag does not verify is discarded and counted as a tamper event (super::HashMetricsSnapshot::tamper_events); the file is simply hashed again, so a tampered store can never turn a deny into an allow. The key inside the record is covered by the tag, so a valid record cannot be moved onto another file, and an old record for the same file carries an old change stamp, so it misses.

§Verify-on-launch

HashVerifyMode is the policy setting that says when a cached digest may be used at execution time. hash_through puts it all together: it stamps the file, uses the cache when allowed, otherwise hashes, checks the file did not change while it was read (retrying up to MAX_UNSTABLE_RETRIES times, then Through::Unstable), and caches the result.
